subject: English
title: The Frog's Great Leap
hook: A frog dreams big. Against all odds, he learns that courage and determination can overcome any obstacle.

slides.title: The Frog's Great Leap
slides.inSimpleWords: A story about dreams, courage, and never giving up.

slides.title: A Frog's Dream
slides.storyContext: A young frog sits at the bottom of a deep well. He looks up at the tiny circle of sky above. 'I want to reach that sky,' he whispers.
slides.inSimpleWords: Big dreams start in small places.

slides.title: The Impossible Well
slides.storyContext: The well is very deep. The frog is very small. Other frogs laugh: 'You'll never jump that high. You'll always be here.'
slides.inSimpleWords: Others doubt, but the frog believes.

slides.title: What is a Dream?

points.label: A dream is
points.text: A hope or wish for something you want to achieve in the future

points.label: Dreams can be
points.text: Big or small, simple or difficult, but they all start with believing in yourself

slides.inSimpleWords: Dreams are the goals we set for ourselves.

slides.title: The First Leap
slides.storyContext: The frog gathers all his strength. He jumps! Higher, higher... but falls back down. He doesn't give up. He tries again. And again.

points.label: Courage means
points.text: Trying even when you might fail

points.label: Determination means
points.text: Standing up each time you fall

slides.inSimpleWords: Failure is just practice.

slides.title: Learning From Falls
slides.storyContext: Each jump teaches the frog something. His legs grow stronger. His hope grows deeper. He remembers: every fall brings him closer to success.

example.problem: What if I keep failing at something I want?
example.solution: Keep trying. Each attempt makes you stronger and smarter

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice makes perfect.

slides.title: Why People Doubt

points.label: Doubt comes from
points.text: Fear and disbelief in what seems impossible

points.label: But remember
points.text: Other people's doubts don't define what you can do—only you do

slides.inSimpleWords: Others' doubts are not the truth.

slides.title: The Breaking Point
slides.storyContext: After many days, the frog is exhausted. An old frog appears and says: 'I failed many times too. But I kept jumping. You can too.'

points.label: The elder's wisdom
points.text: Even the wisest had to fail first to learn

points.label: Hope restored
points.text: Your struggle is not a sign of weakness—it's proof of your strength

slides.inSimpleWords: Never give up on your dream.

slides.title: When You Feel Like Giving Up

example.problem: I've tried so many times and I'm tired. Should I quit?
example.solution: When you feel like quitting, remember the frog. Rest if you need to, but keep your dream alive. The next try might be the one that works.

slides.inSimpleWords: Rest doesn't mean giving up.

slides.title: The Final Jump
slides.storyContext: With renewed energy, the frog takes a deep breath. He jumps with all his might. Up, up, up! His head breaks through the circle of sky!
slides.inSimpleWords: Dreams come true with hard work.

slides.title: Victory Defined

points.label: True victory is
points.text: Not just reaching the goal, but becoming stronger through the journey

points.label: The frog won because
points.text: He believed, he tried, and he never let others' words stop him

slides.inSimpleWords: Success is more than reaching an end.

slides.title: Real-Life Leaps

example.problem: How does the frog's story apply to my life?
example.solution: Whether you're learning math, making a friend, or learning a sport—you're climbing a well. Some days you leap forward, some days you slide back. Keep jumping.

slides.inSimpleWords: Your own well has its own shape.

slides.title: What's Your Well?
slides.storyContext: What dream feels impossible to you? What obstacle stands in your way? How will you be like the frog and keep jumping?

points.label: Your challenge
points.text: Choose one goal and work toward it every day, no matter how small the progress

slides.inSimpleWords: You too can leap beyond limits.

slides.title: Build Your Action Plan

points.label: Step 1
points.text: Write down your goal (your sky above the well)

points.label: Step 2
points.text: List 3 small actions you'll take each week

points.label: Step 3
points.text: When you fall, stand up and jump again

slides.inSimpleWords: Plans turn dreams into real progress.

slides.title: The Frog's Gift
slides.storyContext: The frog reached the sky because he believed. He jumped when others doubted. He rose when he fell. You can do the same.
slides.inSimpleWords: Courage defeats any obstacle.

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Obstacle (barrier), determination (never-give-up spirit), courage (bravery), exhausted (very tired), renewed (given new energy).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: obstacle, determination, courage, exhausted, renewed, strength

slides.inSimpleWords: Words of heroes and dreamers.

slides.title: Three Kinds of Strength

points.label: Physical strength
points.text: Having strong muscles (the frog's legs grew stronger)

points.label: Mental strength
points.text: Having a focused mind (believing in the goal)

points.label: Heart strength
points.text: Having courage and refusing to quit (the frog's spirit)

slides.inSimpleWords: Real strength is more than muscles.

slides.title: When Doubters Become Believers

example.problem: What happens when you finally succeed after everyone doubted you?
example.solution: Sometimes doubters change their minds. But the real win is that YOU believed first—that's what matters most.

slides.inSimpleWords: Your belief comes before others' applause.

slides.title: Spot Courage in Daily Life

points.label: Courage looks like
points.text: Asking a hard question in class, helping someone who's different, trying a sport you're not good at yet

points.label: Find one example
points.text: Where did you show courage this week? Tell someone about it.

slides.inSimpleWords: Courage is everywhere if we look.

slides.title: Different Types of Obstacles

points.label: Obstacles can be
points.text: Physical (a mountain), mental (a tough problem), social (mean people), or emotional (fear)

points.label: Each needs
points.text: A different kind of courage, but the frog's lesson applies to all of them

points.label: Your well
points.text: Is whatever makes you feel trapped. The way out is always through courage and persistence

slides.inSimpleWords: Wells come in many shapes.

slides.title: Real-Life Wells

example.problem: What if my obstacle is different from the frog's deep well?
example.solution: The frog's story isn't just about physical wells. Your well might be shyness, math anxiety, or family problems. The answer is the same: believe, try, keep trying, and ask for help when you need it.

slides.inSimpleWords: Every challenge is a climb.

slides.title: The Role of Small Wins

points.label: Each small jump
points.text: Got the frog closer to his goal and gave him proof he could do it

points.label: Your small wins
points.text: Build your belief. Celebrate them. Every tiny progress counts

points.label: Momentum builds
points.text: From small victories until the big leap becomes possible

slides.inSimpleWords: Small wins compound into big victories.

slides.title: Design Your Own Story

points.label: Your hero
points.text: Create a character (animal, person, or creature) facing their own well or obstacle

points.label: Their journey
points.text: Draw or write what they face and how they overcome it using courage and determination

points.label: The moral
points.text: What does your hero teach us about persistence?

slides.inSimpleWords: Stories help us understand ourselves.

slides.title: The Journey is the Destination

points.label: The frog wanted
points.text: To reach the sky above, but the real prize was who he became

points.label: Your journey
points.text: Toward your goal will change you—build resilience, confidence, and wisdom

points.label: Remember
points.text: The goal matters less than the person you become reaching for it

slides.inSimpleWords: Transformation matters more than achievement.

slides.title: How the Frog Would Help You

example.problem: What would the frog say if I told him I wanted to quit?
example.solution: He'd say: 'I fell a thousand times. Every fall taught me something. You're not weak for struggling—you're strong for trying again. Rest if you must, but don't let doubt win.'

slides.inSimpleWords: Mentors teach through their own scars.

slides.title: Success Looks Different for Everyone

points.label: For the frog
points.text: Success was breaking free from the well and seeing the sky

points.label: For you
points.text: Success might be making a friend, mastering a skill, or standing up for yourself

points.label: The common thread
points.text: Success requires the same courage, determination, and refusal to give up

slides.inSimpleWords: Your well is unique; the lesson is universal.

subject: English
title: Gilli Danda: A Village Game
hook: An ancient Indian game teaches friendship, skill, and the joy of playing outdoors together.

slides.title: Gilli Danda: A Village Game
slides.inSimpleWords: Learn an ancient game from India and its lessons about friendship and skill.

slides.title: An Old Game in a Village
slides.storyContext: In a small village, children gather at sunset with two wooden sticks. Arjun watches as Ravi teaches him gilli danda, a game played for centuries.
slides.inSimpleWords: Ancient games connect us to history.

image.alt: An Old Game in a Village — Gilli Danda

slides.title: What is Gilli Danda?
slides.storyContext: Ravi explains: 'The gilli is a small stick, the danda is bigger. You tap the gilli to make it fly, then hit it far. Try to run and win!'

points.label: The game
points.text: A bat-and-stick game with roots in Indian villages for over 2,500 years

points.label: The rules
points.text: Tap the stick to flip it, then hit it as far as you can. Run and return before others catch you

slides.inSimpleWords: Gilli danda is skill and speed.

image.alt: What is Gilli Danda? — Gilli Danda

slides.title: The Two Sticks

points.label: The gilli (छोटी लकड़ी)
points.text: A small stick, pointed at both ends, that gets tapped and flies into the air

points.label: The danda (बड़ी लकड़ी)
points.text: A larger stick used like a bat to hit the gilli far across the field

slides.inSimpleWords: Simple sticks, endless fun.

slides.title: Arjun's First Try
slides.storyContext: Arjun grips the danda nervously. He taps the gilli. It flies! He swings hard and hits it far across the field. He laughs with joy.
slides.inSimpleWords: Practice brings confidence.

slides.title: How to Play Gilli Danda

example.problem: What are the basic steps to play gilli danda?
example.solution: 1. Place the gilli on the ground. 2. Tap it with the danda so it flies up. 3. Hit it far into the field. 4. Run to a safe spot and back before it's retrieved. 5. If you're tagged, you're out.

slides.inSimpleWords: Every game has simple steps to master.

slides.title: Teamwork and Strategy
slides.storyContext: Ravi teaches: 'Watch your opponent. Learn where they hit. Play as a team. The player who hits farthest and returns safely wins.'

points.label: Skill needed
points.text: Hitting the gilli hard and accurately in one smooth motion

points.label: Speed needed
points.text: Running fast enough to reach safety and return before being caught

points.label: Teamwork needed
points.text: Fielding together to retrieve and tag runners quickly

slides.inSimpleWords: Games teach teamwork and thinking.

slides.title: A Winning Strategy

example.problem: How can I become a better gilli danda player?
example.solution: Practice your tap to control where the gilli goes. Build speed by running daily. Watch where fielders stand and hit away from them. Play with friends more experienced than you.

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice beats talent when talent doesn't practice.

slides.title: Why This Game Matters
slides.storyContext: As the sun sets, Ravi tells Arjun: 'This game connects us to our grandparents and their grandparents. It's part of who we are as Indians.'

points.label: Cultural treasure
points.text: Gilli danda is part of Indian heritage, played across villages for millennia

points.label: Life lesson
points.text: Sometimes the simplest games teach the deepest lessons about courage, skill, and community

slides.inSimpleWords: Games carry culture and history.

image.alt: Why This Game Matters — Gilli Danda

slides.title: Cricket's Ancestor

points.label: Did you know?
points.text: Gilli danda is believed to be an ancestor of the game cricket

points.label: The connection
points.text: Both use a bat and ball (or stick), both require running and strategy, both bring communities together

slides.inSimpleWords: From ancient sticks to modern sports.

slides.title: Learning Sportsmanship

example.problem: What lessons about fair play does gilli danda teach?
example.solution: Respect the rules even when no adult is watching. Celebrate your friends' good plays. Accept losing with dignity. Remember: the game itself is the real victory.

slides.inSimpleWords: Fair play builds real friendships.

slides.title: Play and Learn
slides.storyContext: Arjun challenges his friends to play. They form teams. They laugh. They celebrate. They build memories under the village sky.

points.label: Your turn
points.text: Learn gilli danda or another traditional game. Play with friends. Feel the connection to your heritage

slides.inSimpleWords: Share games, build friendship.

slides.title: Teach Someone Else

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Find a friend or younger sibling who doesn't know gilli danda. Teach them the game like Ravi taught Arjun.

points.label: What you'll learn
points.text: How to explain clearly, patience in teaching, and joy in sharing culture

slides.inSimpleWords: Teaching others makes you a leader.

slides.title: The Physics of the Game

points.label: Angle matters
points.text: How you tap the gilli affects its flight path and height

points.label: Power matters
points.text: The harder you swing the danda, the farther the gilli travels

points.label: Timing matters
points.text: Hitting the gilli at the right moment as it comes down is key

slides.inSimpleWords: Science and skill work together.

slides.title: Reading Your Opponents

example.problem: How do good gilli danda players get even better?
example.solution: By watching how their opponents hit (high, low, left, right) and fielding accordingly. The best players study the game, not just play it.

slides.inSimpleWords: Observation sharpens your game sense.

slides.title: Sunset Wisdom
slides.storyContext: As the game ends, Ravi and Arjun sit together. They realize: the game isn't just about winning. It's about playing together, laughing, and making memories.
slides.inSimpleWords: Games are about joy, not just winning.

slides.title: Traditional Games Around India

points.label: North India
points.text: Gilli danda, kabaddi, kho-kho

points.label: South India
points.text: Pallankuzhi, kabaddi, silambam

points.label: All bring
points.text: Friendship, fitness, fun, and cultural pride

slides.inSimpleWords: Every region has its own treasured game.

slides.title: How Gilli Danda Builds Fitness

points.label: Speed training
points.text: Running back and forth builds leg strength and stamina

points.label: Hand-eye coordination
points.text: Tapping and hitting the gilli improves reflexes

points.label: Agility
points.text: Quick direction changes while running develop balance and control

slides.inSimpleWords: Village games were ancient fitness.

slides.title: Create Your Own Variation

points.label: Challenge
points.text: With your friends, invent a new rule or variation of gilli danda. What would make it more fun or harder?

points.label: Benefits
points.text: Creativity, teamwork, and ownership of your own traditions

slides.inSimpleWords: Innovation keeps games alive.

slides.title: Gilli Danda Teaches Us
slides.storyContext: A simple game with two sticks teaches skill, courage, strategy, and community. It reminds us that the best treasures are time with friends.
slides.inSimpleWords: Traditional games are forever precious.

image.alt: Gilli Danda Teaches Us — Gilli Danda

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Gilli (small stick), danda (larger stick), heritage (cultural inheritance), strategy (game plan), traditional (passed down through time).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: gilli, danda, heritage, tradition, strategy, community

slides.inSimpleWords: Words that celebrate our culture.

slides.title: Why Games Matter Beyond Fun

example.problem: Is there more to gilli danda than just entertainment?
example.solution: Games teach us life skills: how to handle losing, how to work as a team, how to follow rules, and how to respect others. Gilli danda builds character, not just muscles.

slides.inSimpleWords: Games are teachers in disguise.

slides.title: Connection to Modern Sports

points.label: Like baseball
points.text: You hit something and run while others try to catch you or stop you

points.label: Like cricket
points.text: You use a bat, run between bases, and score points

points.label: The difference
points.text: Gilli danda needs almost no equipment—just two sticks and open space

slides.inSimpleWords: Simple games inspire modern sports.

slides.title: Start a Gilli Danda Club

points.label: Step 1
points.text: Find or make two sticks that work as gilli and danda

points.label: Step 2
points.text: Find an open space and invite friends to play

points.label: Step 3
points.text: Document your game (photos or video) and share your heritage with others

slides.inSimpleWords: You can keep traditions alive.

slides.title: How Outdoor Games Shape Character

points.label: Risk-taking
points.text: Running in gilli danda teaches you to take calculated risks and trust your abilities

points.label: Resilience
points.text: You'll make mistakes, get caught, or miss. Learning to bounce back is essential

points.label: Social bonds
points.text: Games build friendships through shared challenge and celebration

slides.inSimpleWords: Play shapes who we become.

slides.title: Leadership Through Games

example.problem: What does a good gilli danda captain do?
example.solution: They encourage teammates, spot each player's strengths, make fair decisions, and play with integrity. These are the same qualities of leaders in any field.

slides.inSimpleWords: Games reveal your leadership style.

subject: English
title: The Raven and the Fox: A Fable of Flattery
hook: A vain raven learns a bitter lesson when a cunning fox uses flattery to steal his cheese.

slides.title: The Raven and the Fox: A Fable of Flattery
slides.inSimpleWords: A timeless fable about pride, flattery, and the cost of vanity.

slides.title: The Prize Cheese
slides.storyContext: A raven sits on a high branch with a piece of cheese in his beak. Below, a hungry fox looks up and smiles slyly. 'What a beautiful raven,' she thinks.
slides.inSimpleWords: Vanity makes us easy targets.

image.alt: The Prize Cheese — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: The Fox's Plan
slides.storyContext: The fox approaches sweetly: 'Dear Raven, I've heard your voice is the most beautiful of all birds. Would you sing for me?'
slides.inSimpleWords: Flattery can hide bad intentions.

image.alt: The Fox's Plan — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: What is Vanity?

points.label: Vanity is
points.text: Excessive pride in your appearance, abilities, or importance

points.label: A vain person
points.text: Believes they are better than others and wants constant praise

points.label: The problem
points.text: Vanity blinds us to reality and makes us vulnerable to deception

slides.inSimpleWords: Pride clouds our judgment.

slides.title: Pride and Vanity
slides.storyContext: The raven's chest swells with pride. He has always wished to be recognized for his beauty and his voice. The fox's words touch his heart.

points.label: What is vanity?
points.text: Excessive pride in one's appearance, abilities, or importance

points.label: The danger
points.text: Vanity makes us believe false compliments and blind us to deception

slides.inSimpleWords: Pride clouds our judgment.

image.alt: Pride and Vanity — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: Recognizing Flattery

example.problem: How can you tell if someone is really complimenting you or flattering you for a reason?
example.solution: Ask yourself: Does this person usually say nice things? Are they asking me to do something unusual? Real friends compliment you; flatterers compliment you when they want something.

slides.inSimpleWords: Real praise doesn't come with hidden costs.

slides.title: The Nature of Flattery

points.label: Flattery is
points.text: Excessive or insincere praise meant to manipulate someone

points.label: How it works
points.text: Flatterers say what you want to hear, not what is true

points.label: The goal
points.text: To make you trust them so they can take advantage of you

slides.inSimpleWords: Flattery is acting, not truth.

slides.title: The Raven Opens His Beak
slides.storyContext: Unable to resist, the raven opens his beak to sing. The cheese falls! The fox catches it and laughs: 'You've been fooled, foolish bird!'

example.problem: Why did the raven fall for such an obvious trick?
example.solution: Because vanity wants to believe compliments, even when they seem too good to be true

slides.inSimpleWords: Vanity leads to our own downfall.

image.alt: The Raven Opens His Beak — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: The Lesson of Flattery
slides.storyContext: The raven realizes too late: the fox didn't care about his voice. She only wanted the cheese. Her words were tricks, not truth.

points.label: About flattery
points.text: False praise often hides bad intentions. Real friends admire you, but don't ask you to sacrifice things

points.label: The moral
points.text: Be wise. Question compliments that ask you to do strange things. A true friend never manipulates you

slides.inSimpleWords: Not all praise is sincere.

image.alt: The Lesson of Flattery — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: Flattery in Real Life

example.problem: Someone says, 'You're so cool, you should skip class with me.' Is this flattery?
example.solution: Yes. They're using flattery to get you to do something wrong. Real cool people make good choices. Don't fall for it.

slides.inSimpleWords: Real friends never ask you to do wrong.

slides.title: Healthy Pride vs. Vanity

points.label: Healthy pride
points.text: Feeling good about your achievements and your effort, without needing others' approval

points.label: Vanity
points.text: Needing constant praise and believing you're better than everyone else

points.label: The difference
points.text: One makes you humble and strong; the other makes you weak and gullible

slides.inSimpleWords: Pride that doesn't need praise is real strength.

slides.title: Spot the Flattery
slides.storyContext: Someone says: 'You're so smart, you could break that school rule without consequence!' How would you respond?

points.label: The answer
points.text: Recognize the flattery. Refuse the trap. Real friends don't ask you to do wrong things

slides.inSimpleWords: Guard against flattery in real life.

image.alt: Spot the Flattery — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: Test Your Wisdom

points.label: Scenario 1
points.text: A new friend says you're talented and asks you to copy homework. What do you do?

points.label: Scenario 2
points.text: Someone compliments your kindness and asks you to join them in leaving a classmate out. What do you do?

points.label: Scenario 3
points.text: A teacher genuinely praises your hard work. How does this feel different?

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice spotting real vs. fake praise.

slides.title: The Difference Between Compliments and Flattery

points.label: A real compliment
points.text: Is specific, honest, and requires nothing from you in return

points.label: Flattery
points.text: Is vague, over-the-top, and often follows a request or precedes one

points.label: Red flag
points.text: If a compliment makes you uncomfortable or seems designed to manipulate, trust your instinct

slides.inSimpleWords: Your gut knows the difference.

slides.title: The Fox's Perspective

example.problem: Was the fox truly mean or just hungry and clever?
example.solution: The fox used deception to get what she wanted, not caring who she hurt. It doesn't matter her reason—using flattery to trick someone is wrong. Character is shown in how we treat others when we're desperate.

slides.inSimpleWords: Desperation doesn't excuse manipulation.

slides.title: The Raven's Wisdom
slides.storyContext: The raven sits alone, sad and wiser. He learns: kindness matters more than compliments. Humility protects better than pride.
slides.inSimpleWords: Humility is our best defense.

image.alt: The Raven's Wisdom — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: The Power of Humility

points.label: Humility means
points.text: Knowing your strengths without bragging, admitting mistakes, and respecting others

points.label: Humble people
points.text: Are harder to trick because they don't need constant praise

points.label: Humility leads to
points.text: Better friendships, real respect, and protection from manipulation

slides.inSimpleWords: True strength is quiet and humble.

slides.title: From Vanity to Wisdom

example.problem: After being tricked, how does the raven grow?
example.solution: By accepting that falling for flattery doesn't make him foolish—it makes him human. He learns to value honest friends who tell him the truth, even if it's not always pleasant.

slides.inSimpleWords: Mistakes are chances to become wiser.

slides.title: Manipulation Tactics and How to Spot Them

points.label: Excessive praise
points.text: Compliments about things nobody usually mentions are a red flag

points.label: Appeal to ego
points.text: 'You're special/smarter/better than others' preys on vanity

points.label: The ask
points.text: Shortly after the flattery comes the favor. That's when manipulation shows itself

slides.inSimpleWords: Know the tricks so you can refuse them.

slides.title: Journal Your Thoughts

points.label: Reflect
points.text: Have you ever felt flattered? Did someone try to manipulate you with nice words?

points.label: Write
points.text: How did you feel when you realized what happened? What would you do differently?

points.label: Learn
points.text: Reflecting on past experiences builds wisdom for the future

slides.inSimpleWords: Learning from experience is true growth.

slides.title: The Fable's Gift
slides.storyContext: The raven and fox teach us: vanity blinds us. Flattery can deceive us. The answer is humility and wisdom.
slides.inSimpleWords: Be humble. Be wise. Be safe.

image.alt: The Fable's Gift — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: New Words Learned
slides.storyContext: Vanity (excessive pride), flattery (false praise), deception (trickery), humility (modesty), slyly (cleverly and sneakily).

points.label: Word bank
points.text: vanity, flattery, deception, humility, sly, manipulate

slides.inSimpleWords: Words of wisdom and warning.

image.alt: New Words Learned — The Raven and the Fox

slides.title: The Ancient Fable Tradition

points.label: Aesop's Fables
points.text: Come from ancient Greece, over 2,500 years old, and teach life lessons through animal characters

points.label: This story
points.text: Has versions in many cultures—French, Indian, and Asian versions all exist with the same core lesson

points.label: Why animals?
points.text: Animals help us see human flaws from a distance, making lessons easier to accept

slides.inSimpleWords: Stories carry wisdom across time.

slides.title: Fables vs. Reality

example.problem: Are fables too simple for real life?
example.solution: Fables are simple on purpose—they show one idea clearly so you remember it. In real life, flattery is often more subtle, but the lesson stays the same: if someone wants something from you and you suddenly hear praise, be careful.

slides.inSimpleWords: Simple stories contain deep truths.

slides.title: Building a Bullshit Detector

points.label: Step 1: Pause
points.text: When someone gives you big praise, pause and think: Why now? What do they want?

points.label: Step 2: Compare
points.text: Does this match what others have said about you? Or is it new and unusual?

points.label: Step 3: Trust your gut
points.text: If something feels off, it probably is. Your instinct is usually right

slides.inSimpleWords: Your instincts are a built-in defense.

slides.title: Find Your Inner Strength

points.label: Reflect
points.text: What compliments do you give yourself when nobody's listening? Those are your real values.

points.label: Write
points.text: Make a list of 3-5 things you know are true about yourself (without bragging)

points.label: Remember
points.text: External praise is nice, but self-knowledge is unshakeable

slides.inSimpleWords: Know yourself before others define you.

slides.title: When Flattery Turns Toxic

example.problem: What if someone keeps flattering you even after you set boundaries?
example.solution: That's not flattery anymore—it's manipulation. Step away from that person. Real friends respect your choices and don't keep pushing once you've said no.

slides.inSimpleWords: Respect means accepting your 'no'.
